review_notes: I read the whole file. It has one definition, `tensorFinStabilization`, and one theorem. The definition is an explicit linear equivalence built from existing Mathlib pieces: `TensorProduct.prodLeft`, `LinearEquiv.rTensor`, `TensorProduct.comm`, `Module.Invertible.linearEquiv` and `prodCongr`. It is specific to this argument and does not stand in for any Mathlib concept. The theorem relies on Mathlib's `Module.IsStablyFree`, `CommRing.Pic` and `free_of_isStablyFree_of_invertible` rather than defining its own versions. The local `exists_finite_free_product_of_finite_projective` in ProjectiveComplement.lean is a standalone existence theorem, not a competing concept, so the rubric excludes it. I did not find a Mathlib definition that this file re-implements. The one remaining uncertainty is that I did not search Mathlib exhaustively for an existing finite-free-complement lemma, and I would not count one as a finding anyway.
